page.layout: Running head at top: "NOTÆ." with page number "148" at left. One text column, full width, with marginal notes in the left margin (an Arabic note beside "lum,*", a note beside "Keblam"). Catchword "plo" at right below the last line.

main_text.p: primum est [?بيان سبب امتزاج النور والظلمة] De-claratio causæ mistionis lucis & Tenebrarum: Secun-dum [?بيان سبب خلص النور من الظلمة] Declara-tio causæ liberationis Lucis à Tenebris, & mistionem istam [?ابتداء] Initium vocant, liberationem [?ارجاع] Redi-tum. Illud quod in ipsorum professione mutaverit Zaradushi hoc fuisse videtur (referente Abulfeda) quòd cùm illo antiquiores Lucem & Tenebras prima rerum principia statuerent, ipse Deum utriusque antiquiorem, earumque conditorem docuerit, unum eum esse nec socium habere, bonum autem & malum,{*}probitatem & nequitiam è commixtura lucis & tenebrarum contigisse, quæ nifi mista fuissent, mundus nequaquam extitisset, nec cessuram mistionem donec lux tenebras vincat, deinde lucem mundum suum, tenebras autem suum, sibi liberum & integrum habituras: Quódque librum religionis præcepta continentem, cùm antea nullum haberent, quasi cælitus ad se demissum, ipsis tradiderit. At mira sunt quæ de libro isto referunt Alsannabius & Ahmed Ebn Tusef. sc. 12. voluminibus, quorum singula corio taurino integro compingerentur constitisse permittit ejus authoritate matrem, sororem, filiam in uxorem sumere (sic & ipse Abulfeda in vita Azdshiri prædicti, cum (quod Magorum instituto licitum) filiam duxisse scribit) cùm aliàs multa in eum è Davidù Psalmis translata sint, Ignis cultum præcepisse, ac Abulfed. in [?كشتاسب] Ine. de opinio-nibus Arabum.Keblam ejus cultoribus Orientem, unde luminarium ortus, statuisse. Simulachris tamen infestum fuisse liquet ex eo quod narrat Sharestanius, Gushtassum postquam Zaradushti suasu, [?Persian: scil.] scil. Magorum doctrinam amplexus esset, Idolis quæ in celebri illo Tem-

page.notes: The Arabic and Persian words in the text and notes are transcribed with [?] because the scan is small and the letters are hard to read exactly; the Arabic glosses may need checking against the original. The asterisk note in the left margin is the Arabic "الصلاح والفساد" (good and evil). The left margin note "Abulfed. in" with its Arabic word and "Ine. de opinionibus Arabum." sits beside the "Keblam" line. The word "plo" at the foot is a catchword completing "Tem-plo" on the next page. No signature is visible. Hyphenation "opinio-nibus" and "Redi-tum" are kept as printed.
